Kiran, you asked about my new headphones? I'm Dhruv, and this is embarrassing.
For months, every video I watched had an advert for the same headphones. Famous singer, slow-motion, city lights. I didn't think about it much. But when my old pair broke, I walked into the shop and picked that brand without even looking at the others.
"These are the best," I told the shop assistant. He asked, "Have you compared the sound?" I said I didn't need to.
Two weeks later, my friend lent me a cheaper pair from a brand I'd never heard of. They sounded better. Clearer bass, more comfortable.
I realised I hadn't chosen quality. I'd chosen the one I'd seen a hundred times. Familiar felt like good.

Nazia, beta, you're buying that phone because it's the one on every billboard? Sit, let your Neelam Khala tell you something.
When I was twenty, I saved for months to buy a pressure cooker. There was one brand on the radio every morning, with a jingle I still remember. I didn't even look at the others. I was sure it was the best, because I'd heard of it a thousand times.

Saturday, late
My colleague Jagdish invited me to a Carnatic music concert tonight. My first thought was: not my thing. I only listen to the same three indie playlists.
Then I wondered, do I actually dislike Carnatic music, or have I just never heard it enough? Maybe what I call my taste is only what I'm used to.
So I made a rule: three fair tries before deciding. Tonight was try one. Honestly, the first half hour felt long and strange. Then a violin part came in and I got goosebumps.
Jagdish lent me two recordings for tries two and three. I'm also trying the Burmese place near office next week, which I've walked past for a year.
I might still not love it. But I'll decide after I've actually met it.
Divyansh
